Works with

Rugged tablet for ServiceNow Field Service Management

ServiceNow Field Service Management is the field service product on the ServiceNow platform, used by organisations that already run ServiceNow for IT, customer service or asset management and want their engineers' work orders in the same system. Dispatchers plan and assign work order tasks in the web interface; technicians receive and complete them in the ServiceNow Agent mobile app, which the documentation also calls Mobile Agent and which appears on the device simply as Agent. ServiceNow's Field Service mobile documentation lists what a technician does in it: accept or reject tasks and plan the day, find routes across several task locations and navigate from the task map, locate parts on an asset map and record assets used, take a customer signature on the device, and search knowledge articles. Tasks done offline are stored on the device and synchronised when it reconnects.

Unusually for enterprise software, ServiceNow publishes a device page for its mobile apps and keeps it current: a table of the minimum Android and iOS version for each app version, a statement of which Android releases are supported, a recommended RAM figure, and a list of tested devices. For the app versions current in 2026 the Android minimum is 12.0, the recommended RAM is 8GB, and the page says plainly that Android tablets are not officially tested. The app itself is published for iOS and Android only, so a Windows tablet reaches ServiceNow through the browser, where the Zurich release supports Edge and Chrome on the desktop.

This page sets out what ServiceNow publishes about the devices its app runs on, which Tuga rugged tablets meet those published figures and where each falls short, why the Tuga A10 is the primary pick, when the Tuga A6 or W10 is the better buy, and how a UK team can buy a single trial unit before committing to a fleet. ServiceNow is licensed to the organisation, not bought with the device, so this is a page for teams that already have it.

Requirements

What ServiceNow Field Service Management (ServiceNow Agent mobile app) needs from a device

Each item below comes from ServiceNow, Inc.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 12.0 minimum for the current app versions (20.4 and later, through 22.x)

    ServiceNow's Tested devices and supported versions page for the Zurich release (updated 30 July 2026) gives a table of minimum operating system versions by mobile app version: 12.x to 12.4 needed Android 7.0, 12.5 to 15.2 Android 8.0, 15.3 to 16.x Android 9.0, 17.x to 18.x Android 10.0, 19.x to 20.3 Android 11.0, and 20.4 and later, 21.x and 22.x Android 12.0 (Snow Cone). The minimum iOS for the same versions is iOS 18. The page also says the mobile apps require the Madrid release of ServiceNow or later and are not forward compatible with older instances. Source: servicenow.com

  • The latest four Android versions are supported

    The same page states that ServiceNow supports the latest two versions of Apple iOS, and the latest four versions of Google Android, and that it reserves the right to re-evaluate support based on OS capabilities and the product roadmap. Read with the table above, the app installs on Android 12 but the supported window is the four most recent releases, so a device on Android 12 or 13 sits below that window while a device on Android 14 or 15 is inside it as of October 2026. Check the current Android release when you buy. Source: servicenow.com

  • 8GB RAM recommended for Android devices; Android tablets not officially tested

    The page says the minimum recommended RAM for Android devices is 8GB. Its tested Android list is made up of Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones plus the Zebra TC51 handheld, and it states that Android tablet is not officially tested. From app version 20.4.0 the platform no longer supports the Intel x86 and x86_64 architectures for Android, so the device needs an ARM processor. Source: servicenow.com

  • Android app from Google Play, for phones and tablets, with offline, navigation, barcode scanning and signatures

    The Android app is published on Google Play as ServiceNow Agent (package com.servicenow.fulfiller, developer ServiceNow). When checked on 25 October 2026 the listing showed an update date of 2 October 2026, a current version in the 22.x line, and device chips for Phone and Tablet. The listing text says agents use the app to accept and update work even without Internet connectivity, that it uses native device capabilities for tasks like navigation, barcode scanning or collecting a signature, and that it ships with workflows for Field Services among others. The listing did not display a Requires Android figure in our check, so the governing figure is the documentation table above. Source: play.google.com

  • Offline mode must be switched on by an administrator, app-wide and per screen

    ServiceNow's offline documentation (Brazil release, updated 10 September 2026) says the apps that can work offline are the Mobile Agent app, Now Mobile app or a custom branded app, that offline mode must be enabled at the app level, and that every screen and function involved must also be configured as available offline. The offline capabilities page (same release and date) sets the limits: list and calendar screens set as available offline are limited to 1000 records, record screens are limited to cached records, and adding attachments or comments offline requires a scripted write-back action. The Field Service mobile page says the data for tasks performed offline is stored on the device and synchronised when the device goes online. Source: servicenow.com

  • Barcode scanning through the camera, with Zebra scanning devices supported on Android

    The Mobile barcode scanning page (Zurich, updated 31 July 2025) lists the formats the apps read on both platforms: 1D EAN-13, EAN-8, UPC-A, UPC-E, Code-39, Code-93, Code-128, ITF and Codabar, and 2D QR Code, Data Matrix, PDF-417 and Aztec, with further formats on iOS only. It states that the Android version of ServiceNow mobile apps can be used with most Zebra scanning devices, notes that Code-128 and Code-39 scanning is not consistent on Android devices due to a known open issue with Android libraries, and points to the EnableCameraFocusEnhancement and EnableMaxCameraResolution mobile properties for better camera scanning. Source: servicenow.com

  • Windows: browser access only, Edge or Chrome on the desktop

    ServiceNow publishes no Windows app for technicians. Its Zurich browser support page lists Microsoft Edge (Chromium) and Chrome at the latest public release and the two previous releases for the desktop interfaces, and marks the Next Experience and Workspace interfaces as not supported on tablet and mobile browsers. A Windows 11 Pro tablet running desktop Edge or Chrome therefore reaches the dispatcher and back office screens; it does not run the Agent app. Source: servicenow.com

Setting up

Getting ServiceNow Field Service Management (ServiceNow Agent mobile app) running

  1. Ask your ServiceNow administrator to confirm the instance is on a supported release (the mobile apps need Madrid or later and are not forward compatible), that the Field Service Management mobile experience is active, and that your technician role has the work order task screens assigned.
  2. On a Tuga A10 or A6, open Google Play and install ServiceNow Agent (package com.servicenow.fulfiller, developer ServiceNow). The app appears on the device as Agent. Enter your instance address and sign in the way your administrator has configured, by password or single sign-on.
  3. Allow location and camera when prompted: the task map, routing and the location tracking feature need location, and barcode scanning, photos and attachments need the camera. ServiceNow documents location tracking as a record of where an agent last worked on an instance.
  4. If your technicians work without signal, have the administrator enable offline mode for the Mobile Agent app and configure each work order task screen and function as available offline; ServiceNow states that the app-level setting alone does not make screens work offline. Open the app online first so the offline data downloads, and keep list screens under the 1000 record limit.
  5. For asset and part barcodes, ask the administrator to add the EnableCameraFocusEnhancement and EnableMaxCameraResolution mobile properties ServiceNow recommends for Android camera scanning, and test Code-128 and Code-39 labels on a trial unit, since ServiceNow notes those are inconsistent on Android.
  6. Run one real task end to end on a trial unit, online and then offline: accept it, navigate from the task map, record a part, take a photo, capture a signature and close the task, then confirm it synchronises and appears for the dispatcher before ordering for the team.
  7. Fit the tempered glass screen protector before the device goes out. For the A10 add the vehicle mounting dock in the van and the charging dock where devices live overnight; for the A6 add the belt holster.

Questions

ServiceNow Field Service Management (ServiceNow Agent mobile app) on a Tuga device

ServiceNow publishes Android 12.0 as the minimum for its current app versions, supports the latest four Android versions, and recommends 8GB of RAM. The Tuga A10 runs Android 14 with 8GB of RAM and 128GB of storage, so it meets each published figure. ServiceNow also says Android tablets are not officially tested, and we do not describe any device as tested or certified by ServiceNow; these are the vendor's published requirements set against the device specifications, and a trial unit with your own instance is the way to confirm it.

Android 12 is the minimum in ServiceNow's version table, so the app installs on it, but the same page says ServiceNow supports the latest four versions of Android, which as of October 2026 means Android 14 and later. The A8 also has 6GB of RAM against the recommended 8GB. It is the brightest screen in the range at 1000 nits and the best outdoor tablet we sell, so if your instance is already in use on Android 12 devices and your administrator is happy, it will work today; we do not recommend it on the published figures because it sits below the supported window.

Yes, once your administrator has switched on offline mode for the Mobile Agent app and configured the screens and functions your technicians use as available offline. ServiceNow's offline pages set the limits: list and calendar screens hold up to 1000 records offline, record screens show cached records, and adding comments or attachments offline needs a scripted write-back action. Work done offline is stored on the device and synchronised when it reconnects. Both the A10 and A6 have dual SIM 4G, so signal gaps are shorter in the first place.

ServiceNow's apps scan 1D and 2D barcodes through the camera, including EAN, UPC, Code-128, QR and Data Matrix, and ServiceNow says the Android apps can be used with most Zebra scanning devices. The A10 scans with its 13MP camera. The A6 has a built-in Zebra 2D scan engine and side scan keys, but the Zebra device ServiceNow names is the TC51 handheld, not an engine inside another maker's device, so check scanning through the engine on a trial unit and treat the camera as the documented route. ServiceNow also notes Code-128 and Code-39 scanning is inconsistent on Android and recommends two mobile properties to improve camera focus and resolution.

No. ServiceNow publishes the Agent app for iOS and Android only. A Windows tablet reaches ServiceNow through the browser: the Zurich browser support page lists desktop Edge and Chrome at the current and two previous releases, and the Tuga W10 runs Windows 11 Pro, so it opens the dispatcher and Workspace screens that a tablet browser is not supported for. That makes the W10 a device for a mobile dispatcher or supervisor, not for the technician's work orders.

Yes to both. A single trial unit before a fleet order is welcome, and for this software it is worth running your real instance and offline configuration on it, since ServiceNow does not test Android tablets.
